sentences.text: The present appeals are filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the common judgment and award dated 20.04.2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi), Vadodara in MACP Nos.1515, 1516 and 1517 of 1993.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined 2.

The brief facts of the case is that the on 23.04.1993, the deceased and injured persons were traveling by a truck no. AET/7205, which was being driven by Alisab at a moderate speed while proceeding towards Ahmedabad.

When the said truck reached near place of occurrence, a truck NO.
CAM/6668 came from opposite direction i.e.,from Ahmedabad side in rash and negligent manner and in attempting to overtake the foregoing truck, the truck No.CAM/6668 came on wrong side and dashed with the truck No.AET/7205.
Because of heavy impact, both the trucks dashed against each other and both the drivers as well as trucks caught fire.
Hence, they have filed the abovementioned petitions to claim compensation from the respondents jointly and severally.

The MACP Nos.1515 and 1516 of 1993 (First Appeal Nos. 121 and 122 of 2014) were originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- on account of the death of deceased and MACP No.1517 of 1993 (First Appeal No.3107 of 2014) was originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- on account of the injuries received in the motor-vehicular accident.
3.

Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions preferred by the present appellant - original claimant under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant- original claimant entitled to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined Rs.2,64,800/-, Rs.5,38,400/- and Rs.1,46,900/- in MACP Nos.1515/93, 1516/93 and 1517/93 respectively at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petitions till its actual realization with proportionate costs.

4. Heard learned Counsels appearing on behalf of the respective parties.
5.

Learned advocate Mr. Mohsin Hakim, appearing for the appellants, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.
6. The first contention is raised with regard to the issue of negligency in MACP No.121 of 2014.
It is submitted that the tribunal has held the deceased for contributory negligency of 50% and thereby reduced the compensation awardable to that extent.

It is further argued that the tribunal has failed to appreciate the fact that the owner of the vehicle had secured his employee-driver by paying extra premium in the event that even if the driver suffers any injury or expires because of his own negligence, insurance company is liable to pay the amount as per the M V Act.

In First Appeal Nos.121 and 122 of 2014, It is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the Tribunal has erred while considering the income of the deceased only Rs.2000/- per month and bhathha of Rs.600/-.

The tribunal has not appreciated the evidence produced at exhibit 81 i.e.,
the salary certificate, which shows that the deceased was earning Rs.8300/- per month.
It is argued that the income of the deceased is required to be assessed on the basis of salary certificate produced on record.

To substantiate his argument on the income aspect, he has placed reliance on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of (I) Mohd. Ameeruddin and Another Vs. United India Insuraunce Company Ltd and Anr (2011) 1 Supreme Court Cases 304 and (II) Rajwati @ Rajjo Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd with Seema Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd 2022 (0) AIJEL SC 70210.

First Appeal No.121 of 2014 12.

Sofar as the contention raised with regard to the issue of negligency, the Tribunal, while deciding the issue of negligence, has recorded a finding of 50% contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and 50% negligence of the driver of the opponent vehicle, relying upon the complaint,
coupled with panchnama and oral evidence of the injured witness ie. the appellant in First Appeal No.3107 of 2014 and other materials on record.

Considering the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay Vs. Laxman Iyer and Anr reported in (2003) 8 Supreme Court Cases 731, it is well settled that in the case of contributory negligence,
courts have power to apportion the loss between the parties as seems just and equitable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apportionment in that context means that damage is reduced to such an extent as the court thinks just and equitable having regard to the claim shared in the responsibility for the damage.

On perusal of the documentary evidences available on record and the findings recorded by the tribunal while dealing with the issue of negligency, this Court also finds that the said apportionment is in consonance with the factual matrix NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined emerging from the panchnama of the scene of accident, complaint, oral evidence of the witness and other materials available on record.
Hence, the findings of the composite negligency of 50% recorded by the tribunal is just and proper and requires no interference.

13. As regards the findings of the tribunal on assessing the income of the deceased is concerned, the wife of the deceased stated in her oral evidence that he was earning Rs.3000/- per month besides other allowances including bhattha and commission Rs.2100/- and Rs.2000/- per month respectively.

The claimants have also produced salary certificate at exhibit 81, which reveals salary of Rs.3,000/- per month, Rs.2100/- towards food allowances, Rs.2000/- towards safety of goods and Rs.1200/- towards bhattha i.e., Rs.40/- per day, which comes to Rs.8300/- per month.
The said certificate was produced in the year 2007 i.e. 14 years after the date of accident.
The year of accident is 1993 and the deceased was working as a driver.
On comparison of the income mentioned in the salary certificate and the rates of driver in the year 1993, there is significant difference.
The income in the salary certificate is excessive and unrealistic noticing the year of accident and rates of skilled workers in that year.

On the other hand, the tribunal is has consider monthly income of Rs.2000/-
per month and Rs.600/- as a bhattha.
It is true that in motor accident claim cases, the tribunal is Alisab Fakir/Shaikh vs Shahebjankhan S-O Haji Abdul ...

The Court can take a reasonable and pragmatic view of the matter.
Having regard the fact that the claimant was engaged in skilled profession of driver, the income assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side.

Noticing the year of the accident, deposition of the wife of the deceased and the judgments relied upon by the appellants,
this court finds it reasonable to assess the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.3500/- per month,
which strikes a balance between the exaggerate claim of Rs.8300/- an the inadequate figure of Rs.2000/- and Rs.600/- bhattha adpoted by the tribunal.
Accordingly, income of Rs.3500/- per month inclusive of bhatthas would serve the ends of justice for the purpose of computation of compensation.

opennyai_summary.facts:
When the said truck reached near place of occurrence, a truck NO.
CAM/6668 came from opposite direction i.e.,from Ahmedabad side in rash and negligent manner and in attempting to overtake the foregoing truck, the truck No.CAM/6668 came on wrong side and dashed with the truck No.AET/7205.
Because of heavy impact, both the trucks dashed against each other and both the drivers as well as trucks caught fire.
The MACP Nos.1515 and 1516 of 1993 (First Appeal Nos. 121 and 122 of 2014) were originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- on account of the death of deceased and MACP No.1517 of 1993 (First Appeal No.3107 of 2014) was originally filed seeking compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- on account of the injuries received in the motor-vehicular accident.
3.
The appellants- original claimant NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined are held entitled to compensation of an amount of Rs.5,39,228/-.
Since by impugned judgment and award the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.2,64,800/-, the appellants shall be entitled to enhanced amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.2,74,500/-
(Rs.5,39,228/- - Rs.2,64,800/-) with interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing of claim petition till its actual realization on the enhanced amount.
Considering the minimum wages of the unskilled workers in the year 1993 ie.,
Rs.900 per month, and the salary stated in the claim petition as well as in the salary certificate, the tribunal has made no error in assessing the income of Rs.1500/- per month and no interference is required with the finding of the tribunal as far as income of the appellant is concerned.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Considering the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay Vs. Laxman Iyer and Anr reported in (2003) 8 Supreme Court Cases 731, it is well settled that in the case of contributory negligence,
courts have power to apportion the loss between the parties as seems just and equitable.
Apportionment in that context means that damage is reduced to such an extent as the court thinks just and equitable having regard to the claim shared in the responsibility for the damage.
On perusal of the documentary evidences available on record and the findings recorded by the tribunal while dealing with the issue of negligency, this Court also finds that the said apportionment is in consonance with the factual matrix NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined emerging from the panchnama of the scene of accident, complaint, oral evidence of the witness and other materials available on record.
Hence, the findings of the composite negligency of 50% recorded by the tribunal is just and proper and requires no interference.
The income in the salary certificate is excessive and unrealistic noticing the year of accident and rates of skilled workers in that year.
Accordingly, income of Rs.3500/- per month inclusive of bhatthas would serve the ends of justice for the purpose of computation of compensation.
For the very same considerations, while the income claimed by the claimant appears on the higher side and the income adopted is on the higher side and the income assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side, therefore,
it is reasonable to assess the monthly income of the claimant at Rs.3500/- per month, which strikes a balance between the exaggerate claim of Rs.8300/- an the inadequate figure of Rs.2000/- and Rs.600/- bhattha NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined adpoted by the tribunal.
Considering the fact that the deceased was survived by four dependents, as per the ration laid down in the decision of Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, 1/4th deduction is required to be applied towards spend by the deceased on himself.
27. As regards future rise of income is concerned, the age of the appellant, the injury sustained by him and nature of his work is required to be taken in to consideration.
Looking to the nature of his injuries, it is clearly evident that the appellant would not be able to do his work normally, which he was able to work prior to the accident.
It is also to be noted that serious injuries inflict lasting mental and emotional scars, beyond physical harm and it deeply alters quality of life.
Therefore, it is the duty of the Court to place victim close as possible to their pre-accident lives and therefore,
considering the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pappu Deo Yadav V. Naresh Kumar and ors reported in 2020 ACJ 2695 and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/121/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined Insurance Company Ltd Vs. Pranay Sethi, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 noticing the age of the deceased as 30 years
So far as the compensation under the other heads such as pain, shock and suffering and special diet, attendant charges and transportation are concerned, considering the facts of the case, nature of injuries, medical treatment and physical pain and the emotional trauma endured by the appellant, a substantial enhancement under the abovementioned heads are deserves to be enhanced.
